<h1>Understanding how models <span>move information.</span></h1>

<p class="hero-lede">
I’m Yingjie Tan. I study the mechanisms that let language models retrieve,
route, compress, and transform information—and how to make those mechanisms
more interpretable and efficient.
</p>

<p class="section-number">01</p>

## Current questions

<p>The themes that organize my experiments, essays, and reading notes.</p>
:::

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-card}
<span class="card-index">A</span>

### Information flow

Which representations and computational paths actually control a model’s
answer?
:::

::: {.research-card}
<span class="card-index">B</span>

### Sparse attention

What gets selected, what gets missed, and why can reasoning still succeed?
:::

::: {.research-card}
<span class="card-index">C</span>

### Efficient context

How can long trajectories and KV caches be compressed without losing evidence?
:::
:::

  <div class="atlas-copy"><span class="atlas-index">03 · COMPRESSION</span><h3>Compression as intelligence</h3><p>KV-cache compression asks what can be discarded, what must remain addressable, and whether useful abstraction is itself a form of intelligence.</p></div>

</article>
